problem: Embodied navigation agents are trained under the action-stability assumption (each discrete action has a fixed, known effect), so they fail badly when action impacts change at test time (e.g. wet floor, broken wheel, disabled actions). Domain randomization only yields conservative policies, and meta-RL, RMA and model-based baselines still fail on severe drifts.
motivation: Real robots face wear, load and terrain changes that alter what actions do, and humans adapt to such changes without retraining. The authors want an agent that fully exploits its changed actions (e.g. reach the goal faster if move-ahead goes twice as far) rather than acting conservatively. Their observation is that linear actor-critic heads tie each output to a fixed action index and so bake in action semantics, which blocks adaptation.
key_idea: Embed each action's impact on the fly from observed state changes (with no action-identity information) and choose actions with a transformer-based, order-invariant policy head over those embeddings.
insight: Generalization to unseen drifts comes from removing action semantics at both stages: embeddings carry only observed impact, and the weight-shared, positional-encoding-free transformer head has no per-action weights. In the PointNav ablation, the Action-Semantics variant (OI head, no action-impact encoder) degrades as drifts grow. The LAC variant (linear head on impact embeddings) performs poorly, so the two modules are complementary. The cost is that AAP starts with identical embeddings and must spend steps exploring action effects, so its SPL and episode length are worse than baselines at modest seen drifts.
method: State encoder: CLIP-pretrained ResNet-50 on RGB plus an MLP goal embedder (GPS/compass for PointNav, object-category token for ObjectNav), concatenated into hidden state h_t.

Action-impact encoder: builds a state-change feature f_t from consecutive observations (o_t, o_{t+1}) and the goal. A shared GRU updates the per-action memory selected by the previous action a_{t-1}, giving embedding e_{i,t}. All embeddings are identical at episode start and carry no action semantics.
Action-Order Encoder: gives the End action a unique, semantics-bearing embedding, because End is unaffected by actuator drift.

Order-Invariant (OI) head: a 6-layer, 16-head Transformer encoder without positional encoding over tokens [e_0..e_n, belief b_t]. A shared feed-forward layer maps action tokens to logits and the belief token to the value.
Policy network: a GRU over the state encoding gives the belief b_t, which is fed to the OI head together with the action embeddings.

Training: DD-PPO plus an auxiliary MSE forward-prediction loss (alpha=1) that predicts the agent state change Δs from each action embedding, trained with small drifts (movement ±0.05 m, rotation ±15°).

Drift protocol: a movement drift d_m and a rotation drift d_r are fixed per episode. Training draws them from a small range, while evaluation uses disjoint, larger unseen values, including disabled rotation actions.

setting.backbone: CLIP-ResNet-50 + GRU + 6-layer Transformer OI head (trained with DD-PPO from scratch, CLIP encoder pretrained)
setting.training_data: RL in RoboTHOR (75M steps PointNav, 200M steps ObjectNav) with small sampled action drifts; ProcTHOR-10k for the real-world ObjectNav model; Gibson v1 for Habitat PointNav
setting.observation: egocentric RGB plus GPS/compass (PointNav) or goal object category (ObjectNav)
setting.action_space: 16 discrete actions: Move(0.05/0.15/0.25 m), Rotate(0, ±30..±150, 180°), End
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR/RoboTHOR (main), modified Habitat-Lab v0.2.1 (Gibson), modified PettingZoo MPE
setting.privileged: none (GPS/compass provided as task goal for PointNav; training uses ground-truth state changes for the auxiliary loss)

numbers_note: Main drift-sweep results (SR/SPL vs. movement and rotation drift for PointNav and ObjectNav, ablations, MPE and Habitat) are given only as figures, so no exact values could be extracted. The text says baselines reach SR≈100% (PointNav) and ≈46% (ObjectNav) on seen drifts while AAP stays roughly constant across drifts.
results: AAP keeps success rate roughly constant across unseen movement and rotation drifts, while EmbCLIP, Meta-RL, RMA and Model-Based drop sharply. With disabled rotations on PointNav, AAP reaches 96.0/98.0% SR versus at most 29.2% for the best baseline (Meta-RL). On ObjectNav it beats baselines by at least 12.5% on average. In the real-world RoboTHOR test it achieves 65% SR versus 25-30% for EmbCLIP.
limitations: Performance degrades for very large movement drifts (e.g. d_m=0.4 m) because movement magnitude is unbounded and training outcomes only cover about [0, 0.3] m.
AAP must first explore to learn action effects, so it has worse SPL and longer episodes than baselines at modest or seen drifts.
The real-world evaluation is small (20 episodes) and only exploratory, and the drifts are injected artificially into commands.
